method: node --import tsx scripts/measure-lifecycle-interleaved.mts --baseline-root=<isolated 1d599fcd checkout with its own npm ci> --phase=tools|hooks --samples=N. Baseline and candidate alternate in AB/BA pairs on one machine with nothing else running (no test suite, no build); a fresh private Git clone and child process per observation; OS page cache not cleared. Tools: two workers, no host/model calls. Hooks: real arbitration with an in-memory session. p50/p95/p99 per operation from the harness's own summary records; every raw sample is included below.
requirement: Lifecycle tools within 20% of 1d599fcd; hooks no slower.

tools-20.fixture: fresh private Git clone and child per observation; alternating AB/BA pairs; OS page cache not cleared; one child at a time; hooks use real arbitration with in-memory session; tools use two workers, no host/model; collect applies one file with keep=true; spawn admission excludes checkout and host launch

roomDoneBreakdown.method: A diagnostic copy of the harness's tools fixture (60 fresh processes each, same warm-up: room_state twice, room_send), timing the lead's room_done with the gate facade's admit/finish/observe wrapped, every synchronous fs call timed, GC from a PerformanceObserver and the main-thread block from monitorEventLoopDelay. 'first': room_done is the process's first admission, as in the harness. 'premarked': one empty admission runs first, so room_done's admit no longer writes the registration's durable hasHeldTickets marker.
roomDoneBreakdown.finding: room_done's own main-thread synchronous work is ~13 ms on both revisions (no GC, ~1.2 ms synchronous fs). The slice-2 cost is the admission: admit ~1.0 ms and finish ~0.15 ms at p50. Its tail (admit up to 9.8 ms) is the first admission's durable hasHeldTickets marker (registration rewrite with fsync in the gate worker); with the marker already written, admit stays within 1.13 ms. That fsync is required by the cheap-ticket design (the marker must be durable before the first unsynced ticket is published) and is paid once per MCP process, on its first admitted operation.
